subject.title: fix: allow bailian provider in resolveThinkingProfile

question: Should OpenClaw accept `bailian` as a special-cased Qwen-compatible provider id in generic configured-model inference, or require this behavior to live only in Qwen/Bailian provider-owned surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is real, but accepting a provider-specific id in generic agent inference is a product and owner-boundary choice with upgrade impact for existing custom configs.

options.title: Accept Narrow Custom-Provider Inference
options.body: Land the generic configured-model inference change after removing the vLLM policy branch, adding focused tests, and receiving proof that exercises a config without explicit `reasoning`.

options.title: Keep Bailian Provider-Owned
options.body: Reject generic `bailian` inference and route the remaining work through the Qwen/Bailian Coding Plan provider boundary tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/26037.

options.title: Consolidate The Coding Plan Fix
options.body: Ask for one Qwen-owned PR that covers bundled catalog metadata, custom-provider docs, inference, tests, and live Alibaba proof together.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Custom-Provider Inference
recommendation.body: Land the generic configured-model inference change after removing the vLLM policy branch, adding focused tests, and receiving proof that exercises a config without explicit `reasoning`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner from history because they merged adjacent Qwen/vLLM thinking work and authored recent provider updates touching the same product boundary.
